subject_line: The vacant Midwestern lots in Department of Elegy
email_body:
Dear Mary,

I've been reading about Department of Elegy and its dim nightclubs, churning lakes and vacant Midwestern lots, held together by the recurring "Book" poems. I was struck that one reader called it both nostalgic and anti-nostalgic at once.

I'd love to ask how you kept that balance: how you decide when a remembered place gets tenderness and when it gets resisted.

The Author Ledger is an independent project featuring short Author Spotlights. Each portrait is built from a few written questions that you can answer at your own pace, and the full text is shared with you for review before publication.

Would you be open to taking part? No pressure either way.

Best regards,
The Author Ledger
hook_note: Black Lawrence Press describes Department of Elegy (2022) as nightclubs, lakes, vacant Midwestern lots; blurbs cite recurring 'Book' poems and Gailey's 'nostalgic/anti-nostalgic' line. Email seen in search result (UAkron faculty bio + CV).

subject_line: Why The Machine We Trust went to a teaching press
email_body:
Dear Tim,

Congratulations on the Midwest Book Award for The Machine We Trust. I was struck by why you placed your debut with Cornerstone Press: its focus on Midwestern writers, and the fact that it is a teaching press, which matched your own commitment to teaching future writers.

I'd love to ask what it was like to see your first book shaped partly by students and how that touched your teaching.
